title: Managing Joe Williams and the Columbia session
summary: Saunders managed Joe, who had fallen on hard times and sold cosmetics to the chorus girls; the Columbia session and Memphis Slim's song are discussed.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Did Joe work with your band, or was he on the show?
I managed Joe. And, see, and he worked in the show. And I managed him for five years.
Well, where did you find him?
Well, Joe had been singing with --
He'd been around here, right, he worked with Jimmy Noon, he worked with Andy Kirk's band, and then he had some problems. This can be restricted, because maybe he doesn't want it known.

Yeah, emotional problems, and he was a little off, to a certain extent. And then he gave up the singing and he couldn't get a job. And so then he was down by the Savoy, he was selling -- I mean, working in a hamburger joint, and then later he went to work for Fuller Products.
Yeah -- no, no, Fuller Products, he was selling cosmetics and things like that.
Then he started coming around the club because he was selling lipstick and things like that to the girls in the chorus. So when he would come around there,
then at that time, I had just gotten a contract with Columbia, and at that time, the big companies like Columbia and all of them, they --

This was 195-- around -- see, because when I put that 'Hambone' out, that was in 1952. See, so in -- pardon me, this was during that time. So we -- I had some tunes and things, and I asked Jimmy if he wanted to make a session with us and he did. And that was -- and then, in the club, every day the thing that really set him off, well, this is where he created it, right there in the club. That was his big thing, that was his --
Memphis Slim was the first one that started singing, and then later B. B. King made it.
Yeah, right. That was Memphis Slim's number.
